name: June Kent
life: “I still remember a secondhand coat with another girl's ribbon still in it.” Friday often includes a stop at the downtown fountain, where June keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I bought the umbrella secondhand. I've found the aunt who made the dress and she wants to tell me about it.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a soft blue checked shirt and a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. June has an aquiline nose and a square chin, with short copper curls. June raises one eyebrow long before saying yes during a conversation.
personality: June is kind in very practical ways and prickly about being thanked in public. June loves being recognized by the people who notice what happens after the guests have left.
agenda: To meet the aunt who wore the original dress.
family: Howard Starr is June’s half-sibling. June remembers the birthdays. Howard asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *Two names on the chart*, Howard says, “I checked her records at night and thought she was a new arrival despite our daughters sharing a classroom.”
connections: Paul Smith. A child's confusion about ownership leads the secondhand buyer to the aunt who made the first dress.
